clue.text: Prototype of smutty magazine

parts.note: blue means smutty or risqué, as in a blue film
print stands for a printed publication such as a magazine

explanation.surface: A dummy issue of a dirty magazine is being shown around.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a plan or model from which later versions are made, so a prototype.

clue.text: Punch churchwarden in the Tube

parts.note: a punch is a blow
a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe

explanation.surface: A church official is punched on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churchwarden' looks like a parish officer but is a long clay pipe; 'the Tube' is London's Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which darts or air are blown.

clue.text: I broke up naff association of workers

indicators.note: broke into, so the letter I is placed inside
up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: naff means unfashionable or vulgar, which is non-U, not upper-class

explanation.surface: Someone broke up a tacky trade association.
explanation.walkthrough: NON-U, a British term for not upper-class, turned upward gives UNON, which I breaks into.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is an organised body of workers, a trade union.

clue.text: Prior's authority

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, coming before in time
an earlier case or ruling that serves as a guide for later ones

explanation.surface: A monastery prior's power over the brethren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like a monk but is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Precedent as an adjective means earlier, and as a noun an earlier decision cited as a guiding rule.

clue.text: Decline to change one word

definitions.meaning: in grammar, to give the case forms of a noun
to alter the ending of a word to show tense, number or case

explanation.surface: A writer refuses to alter even a single word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refuse but is the grammar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Declining a noun is one kind of grammatical inflection, which alters a word's form.

clue.text: One malt ordered for male supporter

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man at the bar orders a single malt whisky for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A telamon is a carved male figure used as a column to support a structure.

clue.text: Overweight: ' adding a pound is disastrous

indicators.note: adding says the next letters are tacked on after the first piece

parts.note: overweight means fat
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Putting on another pound when you are already overweight would be a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal, by extension, describes anything ruinous or catastrophic, a synonym of disastrous.

clue.text: Married German woman's daughter in swindle

parts.note: Frau is German for a wife or married woman

explanation.surface: A German wife's daughter is caught up in a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud is a deception or swindle.

clue.text: The coach found time passed quickly before the game

indicators.note: before says the earlier pieces come ahead of the word for the game

parts.note: ran means moved quickly
sport is a game or the activity of playing games

explanation.surface: A team coach finds the time flew by ahead of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a sports trainer but is a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a vehicle, an example of transport.

clue.text: Refuse to have very young animals

definitions.meaning: a brood of young born to an animal at one time

explanation.surface: Declining to keep newborn pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter means scattered rubbish and also a set of newborn animals such as puppies.

clue.text: Beast inspected, say, in compound

parts.note: an ox is a beast of burden

indicators.note: say tells us the word for inspected is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: inspected means eyed, looked over

explanation.surface: A farm animal was examined while standing in an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a farmyard enclosure but is the chemical sense; EYED is spoken like IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: Decline to take a role, and go to pieces

parts.note: to decline is to fall, as prices do
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: An actor turns down a role and then has a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall apart is an idiom for losing composure entirely, just as going to pieces is.

clue.text: Waste away without answer for optical problem

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for waste away goes around the other piece

parts.note: to pine is to waste away through longing
a key is the set of answers to a puzzle or test

explanation.surface: Someone is wasting away with no answer to their eye trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink-eye is a common name for conjunctivitis, an inflammation of the eye.

clue.text: Domestic detailed to model for old dressmaker

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the remaining letters are reshaped
detailed read as de-tailed, meaning the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A household servant is assigned to model for an old-fashioned dressmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' removes the C from Domestic, leaving DOMESTI, which 'to model' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a dated term for a fashionable milliner or dressmaker.

clue.text: Priest anointed to confute Calvinist doctrine

indicators.note: to confute is to confound, so the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An ordained priest sets out to refute the teachings of Calvin.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvinism teaches that God has foreordained who will be saved, the belief known by this name.

clue.text: Greatly taken with Open University in renamed development

indicators.note: in says the university letters go inside the other piece
development means the letters of the word renamed are worked into a new form

parts.note: OU stands for the Open University, the UK distance-learning body

explanation.surface: A university has been rebranded in a new scheme and people love it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges RENAMED into ENAMRED, with OU slotted inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamoured means filled with love for, so greatly taken with someone.

clue.text: Sister holding gold in the US treasury

indicators.note: in says the sister-and-gold group sits between the outer words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: holding says the sister letters contain the gold symbol

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A nun keeps gold in America's treasury vaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treasury' looks like a store of money but is a treasury of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book of words grouped by meaning, a treasury of words.

clue.text: Something created in Internet cafe, travelling up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the found letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something was made in a cybercafé while someone was travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' looks like the indicator but supplies letters; the run TCAFETRA spans netcafé and travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by people, something created.

clue.text: Finished exam accurately, say, for ecclesiastical post

parts.note: something finished is past, over and done
an oral is a spoken examination
to the letter means exactly or accurately, the 'say' marking this as a loose hint

explanation.surface: A student finished the exam accurately and then applied for a church job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job but means a piece of mail: a bishop's letter read out to the diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral letter is an official letter from a bishop to clergy and people, a piece of church mail.

clue.text: Ruling in the club: no parking

indicators.note: no says the parking letter is to be left out

parts.note: in the club is British slang for pregnant
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Club rules say there is no parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the club' looks like a venue but is British slang for expecting a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant, so ruling.

clue.text: Flower with old label I corrected

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener corrects an old plant label.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden plant grown for its small blue or white flowers.

clue.text: Half-inch tablet for clearing the ears

indicators.note: the ears are what hear, so these words point to the sound of the phrase rather than its spelling

parts.note: a tablet is a pill, so tablet for gives pill for

explanation.surface: A small tablet is taken to unblock the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-inch' is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, meaning steal; it looks like a measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilfer means to steal small things, which is what half-inch means in rhyming slang.

clue.text: Working, I call round having pressing business

indicators.note: round says the word for call goes around the word for working

parts.note: to ring is to phone or call
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: While at work, someone keeps phoning around about urgent matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' looks like urgent but refers to pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing is the job of pressing clothes, so it is literally a pressing business.

clue.text: Publish thin paper and take time off

indicators.note: take with off further on says a letter is removed
off completes the instruction to remove the letter

parts.note: tissue is a thin soft paper

explanation.surface: Someone publishes on flimsy paper and then takes a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to put it out officially, to publish it.

clue.text: In which readers find touching letters helpful

definitions.text: In which readers find touching letters helpful

parts.words: In which readers find touching letters helpful
parts.note: seems to describe moving correspondence, but the letters are felt by touch: a raised-dot writing system for blind readers

explanation.surface: Readers are comforted by heartfelt correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: This tactile alphabet of raised dots lets blind people read by touching the letters.

clue.text: Not bound to fail, so admitting nothing

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the word for fail takes the nothing letter inside

parts.note: to lose is to fail to win
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sure to fail confesses to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' looks like certain to, but 'Not bound' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means free and untied, not bound.

clue.text: Anticipate engine failure after warning

indicators.note: after says the piece for engine failure comes behind the piece for warning

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning to people ahead
a stall is when an engine cuts out

explanation.surface: A motorist predicts the engine will cut out after a warning light comes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act first and prevent something, to anticipate it.

clue.text: Girl artist clutching carrier

indicators.note: clutching says the artist letters hold the carrier inside them

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A young woman painter is holding on to a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a girl's name, the clue's girl being any name of this kind.

clue.text: It's good to be carried round the hilltop

indicators.note: round says the word for being carried goes around the letter for good

parts.note: to ride is to be carried along, as in a vehicle

explanation.surface: It is pleasant to be carried around the summit of the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the long crest or top of a hill or range.

clue.text: Short-lived fugitive

definitions.meaning: fleeting, quickly vanishing, as in fugitive thoughts

explanation.surface: A runaway who does not last long.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means fleeting or short-lived, and fugitive in its literary sense of passing quickly away.
